title: Paneer Enchiladas
description: Paneer Enchiladas combine flavorful spiced paneer wrapped in soft tortillas, topped with a rich homemade enchilada sauce and melted cheese, then baked until golden. A delicious vegetarian fusion of Mexican flavors with Indian paneer.

ingredients.title: For the Paneer Filling
items: Small red bell pepper, finely chopped – 1
Chili powder – ½ tsp (adjust to taste)

ingredients.title: Other Ingredients
items: Small flour tortillas (or corn, lightly warmed) – 6–8
Grated cheese (Mexican blend, cheddar, or mozzarella) – 1 cup
Optional: sour cream or yogurt for serving

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Filling
steps: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add onions and sauté until translucent. Add garlic and bell pepper; cook 2–3 minutes.
Add crumbled paneer, smoked paprika, chili powder, oregano, and salt. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring gently.
Finish with fresh coriander. Remove from heat.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Make the Enchilada Sauce
steps: In a saucepan, heat olive oil and whisk in flour to form a roux (cook 1–2 min).
Gradually add tomato puree and vegetable broth, whisking continuously.
Add chili powder, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, pepper, and sugar. Simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Assemble the Enchiladas
steps: Spread a thin layer of enchilada sauce on the bottom of a baking dish.
Take a tortilla, fill with 2–3 tbsp of paneer filling, roll tightly, and place seam-side down in the dish. Repeat with remaining tortillas.
Pour remaining sauce over the rolled enchiladas and sprinkle generously with cheese.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Bake
steps: Bake in the preheated oven for 15–20 minutes, or until cheese is melted and slightly golden.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Serve
steps: Garnish with fresh coriander and a dollop of sour cream or yogurt. Serve hot with Mexican rice or a fresh salad.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot with Mexican rice or a fresh salad.
Pair with guacamole, salsa, or refried beans.
Finish with sour cream or yogurt and extra fresh coriander.

chefTips: Use fresh, high-quality paneer and sauté lightly to retain its texture.
Homemade enchilada sauce tastes richer than canned – simmer slowly for depth.
Toast tortillas lightly on a skillet to prevent sogginess after baking.
Add a touch of lime juice to the sauce before baking for bright acidity.
